targets.evidence_quote:
The claim selected for replication from Goerg et al. (2010) is that the discriminating reward
scheme under the production function of complementarity achieves almost maximum efficiency, whereas it leads to significantly lower efficiency rates under the production function of substitutability.
targets.outcome_quote: We recorded an average effort level of 0.595 (s.d. 0.135) in the 345SUB treatment and an average effort level of 0.757 (s.d. 0.279) in the 345COM treatment. A Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test yielded a significant difference: exact p=0.018.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The stated original finding is higher effort under complementarity than substitutability; the replication reports the same direction and a significant difference under its prespecified criterion.
